introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Duration: 1 hour 45 minutes.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: In a closed economy without government where the usual assumptions of the basic Keynesian macroeconomic model apply, consumption is always three quarters of disposable income and consumers have the potential of always consuming one hundred billion FCFA when the size of their current income is zero. All investment expenditures are exogenous and initially planned investment is 3,000 billion FCFA.
incertitudes: Question 5(a)(ii) : le sujet demande le revenu disponible avant que la fonction de consommation soit demandée en (b)(i) ; la consommation autonome (100) et la propension marginale (3/4) étant données dans le préambule, le corrigé résout d'abord l'équilibre Y = C + I = 12 400, puis Yd = Y (pas d'État, donc ni impôt ni transfert).

Question 5(c) : « constant rate of 1/5 » est lu comme un impôt proportionnel de 20 % du revenu, sans transferts ; les dépenses publiques (200) s'ajoutent à l'investissement (3 000) comme dépenses autonomes.

Aucun total n'est imprimé par question (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les points de chaque sous-question (a), (b)... sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties ; la somme des points imprimés de la question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define disposable income. (2 marks)

(ii) Calculate the value of disposable income. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Disposable income** is the **income that households have available to spend or save after paying direct taxes (income tax) and receiving transfer payments** ($Y_d = Y - T + \text{transfers}$).

**(ii) Value of disposable income.** In the original situation the economy is closed and has no government, so there are no taxes or transfers: $Y_d = Y$, the equilibrium national income. Consumption is $C = 100 + 0.75\,Y_d$ (billion FCFA) and investment is $I = 3000$. At equilibrium, $Y = C + I$:

$$Y = 100 + 0.75\,Y + 3000$$

$$0.25\,Y = 3100 \quad\Rightarrow\quad Y = \frac{3100}{0.25} = 12\,400$$

Disposable income is therefore $Y_d = Y = $ **12,400 billion FCFA**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Derive the consumption function of this economy. (2 marks)

(ii) Determine the value of total consumption in this economy. (2 marks)

(iii) List three factors that determine consumption. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Consumption function.** The consumption function has the form $C = a + bY_d$, where $a$ is autonomous consumption (consumption when income is zero) and $b$ is the marginal propensity to consume. The question gives $a = 100$ billion FCFA and $b = \tfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$, so

$$C = 100 + 0.75\,Y_d \quad \text{(billion FCFA)}$$

**(ii) Total consumption.** With $Y_d = 12\,400$ from (a)(ii):

$$C = 100 + 0.75 \times 12\,400 = 100 + 9300 = 9400$$

Total consumption is **9,400 billion FCFA**. Check: $C + I = 9400 + 3000 = 12\,400 = Y$, so the economy is in equilibrium.

**(iii) Three factors that determine consumption** (1 mark each, any three): the level of **disposable income** (the main determinant); the **level of wealth** (houses, savings, shares); the **interest rate and the availability of credit** (higher rates encourage saving); **expectations** about future income and prices; the **distribution of income** (the poor consume a larger share of their income); the **price level** and **taxation**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
If in the original situation income tax was introduced at a constant rate of 1/5 at all incomes together with a planned government spending of two hundred billion FCFA:

(i) Calculate the equilibrium level of income. (4 marks)

(ii) Compute the value of the multiplier. (3 marks)

(iii) State any two factors that can reduce the size of the multiplier. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Now there is a proportional income tax at rate $t = \tfrac{1}{5} = 0.2$ and government spending $G = 200$ billion FCFA.

**(i) Equilibrium income.** Disposable income is $Y_d = (1 - t)\,Y = 0.8\,Y$, so consumption becomes

$$C = 100 + 0.75 \times 0.8\,Y = 100 + 0.6\,Y$$

Equilibrium requires $Y = C + I + G$:

$$Y = 100 + 0.6\,Y + 3000 + 200$$

$$0.4\,Y = 3300 \quad\Rightarrow\quad Y = \frac{3300}{0.4} = 8250$$

The equilibrium level of income is **8,250 billion FCFA**. Check: $Y_d = 0.8 \times 8250 = 6600$, $C = 100 + 0.75 \times 6600 = 5050$ and $C + I + G = 5050 + 3000 + 200 = 8250$.

**(ii) The multiplier.** With a proportional tax the multiplier is

$$k = \frac{1}{1 - b(1 - t)} = \frac{1}{1 - 0.75 \times 0.8} = \frac{1}{0.4} = 2.5$$

The multiplier is **2.5** (it was $\frac{1}{1 - 0.75} = 4$ before tax). Check: autonomous spending is $100 + 3000 + 200 = 3300$ and $3300 \times 2.5 = 8250$. The tax is a leakage, so it reduces the multiplier.

**(iii) Two factors that reduce the size of the multiplier** (any two; 1 mark each): a **higher marginal propensity to save** (lower MPC); a **higher rate of income tax** (a larger leakage); a **higher marginal propensity to import** (in an open economy); and, in practice, supply constraints near full employment (the extra demand raises prices instead of output) and the crowding out of private spending.
